43461701.article_summary: Triforce 是一个为 Apple Silicon 笔记本（如 MacBook Pro 和 MacBook Air 的 M1/M2 系列）麦克风阵列设计的自适应波束成形器。它基于最小方差无失真响应（MVDR）算法，旨在通过用户空间实现信号与背景噪声的分离，解决麦克风阵列过于敏感和全向性的问题。该项目依赖少量外部库，如 LV2，并使用 Rust 编写。由于缺乏 SIMD 优化和宽带分解能力，当前版本在性能和效率上有限，输出为单声道，且无法实时处理立体声。项目代码基于 GPL-2.0 许可发布，并欢迎改进补丁。

不同观点：
• CalRobert认为，Whitecoat行动中的士兵志愿者是在知情并自愿的情况下参与实验的，且实验遵循了适当的伦理程序。他还提到自己曾参与基督复临安息日会的经历，认为该教会在医疗领域有贡献，但也存在一些保守的宗教观念，如年轻地球创造论。他同时表示怀念教会的社区感，并指出当时的教会对婚姻平等等问题持较为开放的态度。

• aredox指出，在同一历史时期，一些实验遵循了伦理程序，而另一些则没有，这反映出即使在当时，人们对于不道德的人体实验也存在反感和抵制。他将Whitecoat行动的伦理实践与其他不道德的实验进行了对比。

• mullingitover认为，基督复临安息日会已经从原本坚定的道德立场（如对堕胎和疫苗的开放态度）转变为与主流右翼福音派相似的立场。他通过自己的经历说明，早期的教会在堕胎等问题上持较为中立的态度，而如今的教会则更多受到社交媒体和极端观点的影响，变得更为保守和激进。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是基督复临安息日会的演变，特别是其在堕胎和疫苗等问题上的立场变化。mullingitover认为，教会已经从原本的“宗派”角色转变为“教派”，在道德立场上做出了妥协以适应主流社会，但如今却越来越接近右翼福音派的立场。

• CalRobert对教会的社区感和音乐传统表示怀念，并认为社会可以从安息日的文化实践中受益。他认为当时的教会对婚姻平等等问题持开放态度，而mullingitover则认为如今的教会已经发生了变化，不再具备这种开放性。

• aredox的评论强调了历史背景下的伦理实践，指出了同一时期不同实验在伦理上的差异，反映了当时社会对实验伦理的不同态度。

data.title: AI browser assistant extensions probably beaming everything to the cloud
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 一篇由多国研究人员撰写的预印本论文揭示，许多作为浏览器扩展的生成式AI助手存在隐私风险，可能会收集和传输用户的敏感数据，包括健康和学生信息，这可能违反美国法规如HIPAA和FERPA。研究分析了十款Chrome扩展，包括Sider、Monica和ChatGPT for Google，发现这些扩展通常将网页内容和用户输入发送至远程服务器，有时甚至共享给第三方追踪器。这些数据可用于定向广告或模型训练，进一步威胁用户隐私。与苹果的局部处理不同，这些扩展大多依赖服务器端API处理数据，增加了信息泄露的可能性。研究强调，用户需警惕这些扩展的数据处理行为。

You know that generative AI browser assistant extension is probably beaming everything to the cloud, right?
15
Just an FYI, like
Thomas Claburn
Tue 25 Mar 2025
//
08:31 UTC
Generative AI assistants packaged up as browser extensions harvest personal data with minimal safeguards, researchers warn.
Some of these extensions may violate their own privacy commitments and potentially run afoul of US regulations, such as
HIPAA
and
FERPA
, by collecting and funneling away health and student data.
A group of computer scientists from University of California, Davis in the USA, Mediterranea University of Reggio Calabria in Italy, University College London in the UK, and Universidad Carlos III de Madrid in Spain set out to analyze the privacy practices of browser extensions that use AI to do things like produce summaries of webpages or answer questions about content.
The academics – Yash Vekaria, Aurelio Loris Canino, Jonathan Levitsky, Alex Ciechonski, Patricia Callejo, Anna Maria Mandalari, and Zubair Shafiq – describe their findings in
this pre-print paper
, titled: "Big Help or Big Brother? Auditing Tracking, Profiling, and Personalization in Generative AI Assistants."
Using
network traffic analysis tools
, such as mitmproxy, the team studied ten generative AI Chrome Extensions: Sider, Monica, ChatGPT for Google, Merlin, MaxAI, Perplexity, HARPA, Wiseone, TinaMind, and Copilot.
Despite the use of familiar terms like ChatGPT, Google, and Copilot in the titles of these extensions, the makers of these extensions are unaffiliated with Google, Microsoft, or OpenAI.
What the academics found is not entirely surprising given the long history of privacy and security problems in the Chrome extension ecosystem. For one thing, this add-on software typically has the power to inspect and modify the pages you visit. In the case of these assistants, they send off your data, such as the webpage you're on, to remote AI services for processing and harvesting. If that page has anything sensitive on it, off it goes into the internet.
When you think about it, the risk seems obvious, but these academics have taken the time to document it so that one no longer has to make assumptions. Which is nice.
"In our study, we emphasize that not only do these assistants collect users' highly sensitive data," Yash Vekaria, a graduate student researcher at UC Davis and corresponding author of the report, told
The Register
Monday, "but that this information is also shared with their own servers as well as third-party trackers, which can be further utilized to target highly personalized and sensitive ads to the user.
"Our paper tries to emphasize that in the age of AI, the already poor privacy of Chrome extensions can be further exploited by generative AI assistants, which can use this information to profile users over time and then personalize their responses for the user – which could be highly sensitive. The data collected about the user could be used by these assistants to further train their models and may have inadvertent consequences."
Rather than using local in-browser models – a capability Apple has touted for its
not-fully-implemented
Apple Intelligence system – most of these (90 percent) third-party AI extensions rely on server-side APIs for processing. And according to the researchers, these APIs might be used by the add-on software without explicit user interaction.
By processing, we mean, you're on a page with the extension enabled, and you type a query into the add-on about the webpage, or you request a task such as summarization, and the data and request are fired off to a remote API, with the results shown in the extension. The issue here is: How much data is sent off, and could anything be done to limit the transfer of sensitive information?
"When invoked, these browser assistants collect and share webpage content, often the full HTML DOM [document object model] and sometimes even the user’s form inputs, with their first-party servers," the researchers state in their paper. "Some gen-AI browser assistants also share identifiers and user prompts with third-party trackers such as Google Analytics."
This information collection and sharing has been documented in some instances on webpages that contain sensitive health or personal information, such as the web forms used to submit medical data or social security numbers.
Vekaria said his group tested the extensions on a university health portal after authenticating with a personal account.
"We observed that full webpage content with HTML DOM (including the user's personally identifiable information, and sensitive health conditions, medical history, etc) was collected by Sider, Merlin, and Harpa; while other extensions (Monica, ChatGPT for Google, MaxAI, and Wiseone) collected textual data in plain text (ie, not HTML; but page text, page title, page URL)."

data.title: NSA warned of vulnerabilities in Signal app a month before Houthi strike chat
data.author: jasoncartwright
data.article_summary: 本文报道了美国国家安全局（NSA）在2025年2月向员工发出的安全警告，指出加密通讯应用Signal存在漏洞，可能被用于拦截敏感信息。这一警告是在《大西洋月刊》披露国防部长佩特·赫格斯意外通过Signal聊天向记者透露对也门胡塞武装的作战计划后发出的。赫格斯在美军行动前两小时，不小心在群聊中分享了有关武器、目标和时间的详细信息。尽管NSA提醒不要在Signal上分享任何非公开信息，但包括国家安全顾问迈克·沃尔兹在内的多名特朗普政府高官被指参与了该聊天。CIA局长和国家情报总监在国会作证时否认聊天中包含机密或敏感的行动细节。此事引发国会民主党人的强烈批评，并要求展开调查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Google上个月报告的攻击是否是NSA警告中所提及的攻击，以及是否应记录通过Signal进行的涉及消失消息的敏感对话。

不同观点：
• 第一个讨论点是确认该攻击是否为NSA警告中提到的攻击。一名用户引用Google的博客和NSA的完整文件链接，确认此攻击正是NSA警告中提到的那个。这表明用户关注具体事件和官方警告之间的关联性。

43475624.article_content:
Latest on Yemen bombing group chat
Latest details on Trump officials' group chat with journalist about Yemen bombing
18:37
The National Security Agency sent out an operational security special bulletin to its employees in February 2025 warning them of vulnerabilities in using the encrypted messaging application Signal, according to internal NSA documents obtained by CBS News.
News of the NSA bulletin comes amid the continued fallout from an explosive
article
published Monday
in The Atlantic. The publication's editor-in-chief, Jeffrey Goldberg, detailed how Defense Secretary
Pete Hegseth
inadvertently disclosed war plans to him in an encrypted
Signal
chat group two hours before the U.S. military launched attacks against Houthi militia in Yemen. Goldberg wrote that Hegseth's messages included "precise information about weapons packages, targets, and timing."
The NSA is an arm of the Defense Department and specializes in signals intelligence — which is derived from electronic transmissions — and cybersecurity. The agency is responsible for monitoring, collecting and processing information and data for U.S. national security interests.
The unclassified but for-official-use-only
documents provided to CBS News
by a senior U.S. intelligence official are entitled "Signal Vulnerability" and were sent out the month before Goldberg was accidentally added to the
group chat
allegedly by national security adviser Mike Waltz.
"A vulnerability has been identified in the Signal Messenger Application. The use of Signal by common targets of surveillance and espionage activity has made the application a high value target to intercept sensitive information," the internal bulletin begins.
The bulletin warned of
Russian
professional hacking groups employing phishing scams to gain access to encrypted conversations, bypassing the end-to-end encryption the application uses.
The bulletin also underscored to NSA employees that third-party messaging applications such as
Signal
and Whatsapp are permitted for certain "unclassified accountability/recall exercises" but not for communicating more sensitive information.
NSA employees were also warned to not send "anything compromising over any social media or Internet-based tool or application," and to not "establish connections with people you do not know."
CBS News contacted the NSA for comment but did not receive a reply prior to publication.
On Tuesday, National Intelligence Director Tulsi Gabbard and CIA Director John Ratcliffe, both of whom were reportedly in the Signal group chat,
testified
before a Senate panel.
"There was no classified material that was shared in that Signal chat," Gabbard told lawmakers. But the NSA bulletin advises that even information that is not categorized as classified should not be shared on Signal, advising users not to share "unclassified, nonpublic" information on the messaging platform.
Ratcliffe said Signal "is a permissible use" application that has been approved by the White House for use by senior officials. The group chat, Ratcliffe said, was a "mechanism for communicating between senior level officials but not a substitute for using high side or classified communications."
Both Ratcliffe and Gabbard were asked by Democratic Sen. Martin Heinrich of New Mexico whether the Signal conversation included information on "weapons packages, targets or timing." Ratcliffe replied, "Not that I'm aware of," and Gabbard said, "Same answer and defer to the Department of Defense on that question." Both said they had no knowledge of the chat including operational details of the strike in Yemen.
Arden Farhi
contributed to this report.

data.author: fliellerjulian
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对职业社交平台（特别是与LinkedIn对比）的功能、设计和用户体验的看法

不同观点：
• **支持简化功能，专注于求职和招聘基本需求**：
  - DeathArrow认为平台应简单直接，只需提供基本的求职和招聘功能，如发布简历和标示求职状态，不需要额外的视频或复杂功能。
  - neilv反对在简历中加入照片，认为这可能导致歧视问题，并指出LinkedIn虽然流行，但也有很多缺点。
  - davedx也反对增加视频内容，认为这不会改善用户体验。

• **支持通过内容和网络效应提升个人品牌**：
  - janalsncm建议通过技术博客或项目展示来突出个人能力，而不是依赖照片或视频。
  - vector_spaces指出算法推荐和活跃用户展示有助于增加平台的社会证明效应，但也提到新用户上手时需要更明确的指引和互动机制。
  - adabyron建议建立有价值的小型讨论组，以促进深度交流，并认为应避免LinkedIn那样的社交feed带来的干扰。

• **对平台设计的不同期望**：
  - oytis质疑设计一个让所有人都“突出”的平台是否可行，认为这样只会增加用户的工作量，且对招聘方也不利。
  - smeej指出LinkedIn对那些职业路径不直线的人不友好，每次修改简历很麻烦。
  - 8mobile希望有一个更简洁的LinkedIn版本，而不是增加更多社交功能。

• **对视觉展示的争议**：
  - neilv和confooseddd都反对在简历或个人资料中过度强调照片和视觉元素，认为工作成果才是关键，平台应专注于客观的内容展示。
  - scosman建议从美观和易用的作品集入手，吸引用户创建和分享个人页面，而不是直接与LinkedIn竞争网络效应。

补充讨论：
• **用户网络与平台吸引力**：
  - iancmceachern指出平台的成功关键在于能否持续吸引新客户，而不仅仅是平台本身的功能。
  
• **其他反馈**：
  - runlaszlorun认为现有职业社交平台如LinkedIn不尽如人意，支持新平台的创建。
  - venusenvy47对URL的误读提供了一个轻松的评论，虽与核心讨论无关，但显示了用户对平台名称和品牌的敏感性。

争议焦点：平台是否应增加视觉和视频内容以帮助用户“突出”，还是应保持简洁、专注于文本和客观成果的展示。

data.title: Microsoft's many Outlooks are confusing users – including its own employees
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 微软的多种Outlook版本让用户感到困惑，甚至连公司员工也不例外。微软老兵Scott Hanselman幽默地建议了一些新变体，如Outlook (Zero Sugar)和Outlook (Caffeine Free)，以突出这一问题。目前，用户可能同时拥有新版Outlook和Outlook (Classic)，后者支持到2029年。尽管微软希望用户转向新版，但新版缺少许多经典版的功能，且不支持企业常用的COM插件。这种多个相似选项并存的情况可能导致用户混淆，并引发管理上的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对微软新旧Outlook及其相关产品的体验和争议

不同观点：
• **支持适应新Outlook的用户**：  
  - 用户[Alupis]提到，虽然新Outlook在界面和功能上有些令人困惑，且部分按钮和选项不够直观，但经过一段时间的适应后，逐渐习惯了这种变化。  
  - 尽管新界面需要重新学习，但这是软件升级的一部分，用户认为可以接受。

• **反对新Outlook的用户**：  
  - 用户[focusedone]强烈批评新Outlook的附件处理方式，尤其是只能将文件保存到OneDrive，而不能选择任意本地位置，严重影响了工作效率。  
  - 用户[mrweasel]表示不理解微软为何不直接提供经典Outlook版本，反而强制推广一个“劣化”的版本，尤其在用户已经为“好版本”付费的情况下。  
  - 用户[deelowe]认为Outlook在处理基本任务时（如搜索、会议安排等）非常混乱，相比Google Workspace，Outlook显得非常糟糕。

• **对微软整体产品策略的批评**：  
  - 用户[transcriptase]对比苹果公司，指出微软缺乏对用户体验的把控，认为微软内部缺乏能够抵制愚蠢和混乱设计决策的人。  
  - 用户[yuters]对微软365（现称为Microsoft 365）的多个版本和命名感到困惑，认为整个产品线极其混乱。

• **技术性问题与漏洞**：  
  - 用户[Kwpolska]提到新Outlook的加载问题，认为一个桌面邮件客户端不应该需要互联网连接才能显示最近的邮件。  
  - 用户[EarthIsHome]指出Outlook通知功能的一个长期未修复的漏洞，即点击通知后邮件会在其他窗口后面打开。

• **对微软生态系统的复杂性感到不满**：  
  - 用户[xg15]提到，任何使用微软账户登录的第三方产品都需要通过多个微软自有域名进行交互，这种复杂的架构让用户体验非常混乱。

• **对经典产品的怀念与其他工具的推荐**：  
  - 用户[vincent-manis]提到自己使用Thunderbird，感觉错过了Outlook发展中的关键历史。  
  - 用户[CrimsonCape]寻找类似于VoidTools 'Everything'的邮件应用，希望有一个专注于速度和功能的邮件客户端，而不是过于注重UI设计。

补充讨论：
- 用户对微软产品命名和版本管理的困惑，如Teams和.NET的命名问题，进一步加剧了对微软整体产品策略的不满。  
- 部分用户提到经典Outlook的功能强大，特别是MAPI编程接口的灵活性，对新版Outlook的“简化”和功能削弱表示不满。

43474707.article_content:
Applications
40
Microsoft's many Outlooks are confusing users – including its own employees
40
Redmond veteran proposes Zero Sugar and Caffeine Free variants
Richard Speed
Tue 25 Mar 2025
//
13:15 UTC
Baffled by the plethora of Outlook options out there? You aren't alone. Microsoft veteran Scott Hanselman posted a list of some more variants that could be used to do the same thing.
It's a problem common to several Microsoft products. A file needs to be opened, but which app should be used? Should it be Outlook New, or Outlook (New)? With tongue firmly in cheek, Hanselman listed some more options: Outlook (Zero Sugar), Outlook (Caffeine Free), and so on.
Hanselman, Developer Community veep at Microsoft, also included Outlook '95, although to our mind the peak came with the version of Outlook in Office 97. A happier, more trusting time when security was less important.
While users can create multiple
Outlook profiles
to store email account details and data locations, Hanselman's
post
on Bluesky highlights an issue facing many users of Microsoft's software: which incarnation of the application to use.
Teams users often find themselves presented with a variety of applications – Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Teams (Personal), for example, can often appear side by side in the system tray.
As for Outlook, users are likely to have multiple versions installed. Microsoft
forced the new version onto devices as part of a Windows update
and renamed the previous version to Outlook (Classic) so the pair could run side by side. While support for the Classic version of Outlook will persist until at least 2029, Microsoft would like users to move to the new version despite it lacking many of its predecessor's functions.
According
to Microsoft: "The new Outlook for Windows, built upon modern service architecture, is inspired by the Outlook web experience." It also does not support the COM add-ins used by many enterprises to glue corporate workflows together.
Oops, they did it again: Microsoft breaks Outlook with another dubious update
Even Windows 10 cannot escape the new Outlook
New Outlook marches onto Windows 10 for what little time it has left
Outlook is poor for those still on Windows Mail, Calendar, People apps by end of year
Currently, the new Outlook is at the opt-in stage and is off by default. It will then proceed to an opt-out stage, where users must actively switch back to the Classic experience before the Cutover stage, after which reversal is no longer possible. Microsoft says it will give administrators at least 12 months' notice before this is implemented in production rings.
Existing perpetual installations of classic Outlook "will continue to be supported until at least 2029,"
according
to Microsoft.
There is a cautionary tale about
what happened
when a soft drinks company tried to replace a well-liked product with a "new" version and renamed the previous preferred version as "classic."
The list posted by Hanselman – who is also
notable
for tips on managing Microsoft's personal information manager – is amusing, but also highlights the perils of having multiple, similarly functioning options to do the same thing, and the potential for confusing users.
Outlook (Stable and Fast) anyone? ®

data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了“首次已知物种照片”项目的最新进展和规则。项目已收集超过7,000个观察记录，成员数突破2,000。文章重申了参与项目的规则：1) 提交的照片必须是该物种在全球范围内的首次照片，而不仅仅是在iNaturalist上的首次；2) 照片必须展示活的个体，不能是空壳、死鱼或昆虫标本等；3) 如果物种的雌雄异形或有不同生命阶段，这些都可以分别提交，但仍需遵循前两个规则。文章还感谢了积极参与项目的用户，特别是对甲虫类观察有突出贡献的borisb。

To my great surprise, I just realised it's been more than two and a half years since I last wrote a journal post for this project! Very lax of me, and apologies to all for the lack of more regular updates.
The project has been surging along, and we now have more than 7,000 observations, which is fantastic to see. We also recently surpassed 2,000 project members, thanks in part to some regular mentions of the project in recent iNat blog posts (eg observation of the week).
So for all the newer members, I'll run through the project rules again:
1 . Any observations you add must be the first photograph(s) of that species anywhere. If an observation is the first one for that species to be uploaded to iNat, but other photos of that species from an earlier point in time already exist anywhere elsewhere online/in print, then that observation should not be added to the project. This is the biggest source of observations that I have to remove from the project. So your observation must be both the first photograph of that species on iNat and also the first anywhere.
If you encounter an observation of a species that is older than one already in the project, add it, but please message me so I can remove the one that no longer qualifies as oldest.
2 . Your photograph must be of a living individual. A number of observations have been added that depict things like empty mollusc shells, dead fishes, pinned insects, etc. Whilst these are of course valuable observations, they are not eligible for the project.
3 . If the male and female of a species are sexually dimorphic, then both are valid to be added to the project. So too if a species has distinct life stages (eg caterpillar/chrysalis/butterfly), they are all valid to be separately added to the project (assuming the other rules apply). Ditto for plants; if one observation shows the first ever photos of flowers, and another the first ever of fruits, they are both ok to add to the project. Please make sure, however, that the first two rules are also followed in these cases.
The project is very much self-sustaining now, with users adding observations to it every day, and there are a number of users in particular who have added many IDs and/or added records to the project, so huge thanks to everyone involved. I'd like to especially highlight the recent efforts of
@borisb
, who has contributed tremendously (IDing and adding) in the world of beetles and has been a very vocal advocate for the project, letting users know each time he adds one of their observations.

data.title: Optimizing ML training with metagradient descent
data.author: ladberg
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种基于元梯度下降（Metagradient Descent, MGD）的方法，用于优化大规模机器学习模型的训练过程。作者提出了一种高效计算元梯度的算法，并引入了一个"平滑模型训练"框架，使得利用元梯度进行有效优化成为可能。实验表明，MGD在数据集选择和抵御数据中毒攻击方面显著优于现有方法，并且能够自动找到具有竞争力的学习率调度策略。该方法为优化模型训练配置提供了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器学习中超参数优化问题的挑战及其与其他工作的比较

不同观点：
• [munchler 的观点] 超参数优化是一个复杂且耗时的过程，特别是在当前的机器学习问题中，涉及十几个简单的超参数，每次训练可能需要数小时甚至数天。他认为，没有对问题领域的深刻理解，很难有效地搜索超参数空间。即使是小的配置调整，也可能导致显著的结果变化，或者导致失败。超参数对性能有直接影响，并且对硬件限制非常敏感，选择不当的超参数可能导致内存不足错误或者极长的运行时间。总体来说，他认为这是一个现实中的“停机问题”。

• [jn2clark 的观点] 他提出了对“学习如何学习”（learning to learn）相关工作的比较，并提供了一篇论文链接（https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04474）。jn2clark 似乎认为 munchler 的问题可能与“学习如何学习”领域的研究有关，并询问为什么没有引用相关工作。

补充讨论：
• munchler 提到，除了超参数优化，还有更复杂的设计决策，比如模型的架构，这些不能简单地通过超参数来捕捉。这表明超参数优化只是机器学习模型设计中的一部分挑战，还有更复杂的问题需要考虑。

• jn2clark 的评论可能暗示“学习如何学习”方法可以提供一种系统化的方式来处理超参数优化问题，但这一点在 munchler 的原始评论中没有被提及或讨论。因此，是否以及如何应用“学习如何学习”方法来解决超参数优化问题是一个潜在的讨论点。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否可以通过“学习如何学习”等方法系统化地解决超参数优化问题，还是需要依赖于对问题领域的深刻理解和经验性的调整。

Abstract:
A major challenge in training large-scale machine learning models is configuring the training process to maximize model performance, i.e., finding the best training setup from a vast design space. In this work, we unlock a gradient-based approach to this problem. We first introduce an algorithm for efficiently calculating metagradients -- gradients through model training -- at scale. We then introduce a "smooth model training" framework that enables effective optimization using metagradients. With metagradient descent (MGD), we greatly improve on existing dataset selection methods, outperform accuracy-degrading data poisoning attacks by an order of magnitude, and automatically find competitive learning rate schedules.

data.title: Ruby, Ractors, and lock-free data structures
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了在Ruby中实现并发数据结构的方法，目标是展示如何在全局可变状态下实现真正的并行处理（当前Ruby内置功能不支持）。文章涉及Ruby、Rust和C等语言，但并非必须精通。示例代码可在GitHub上找到，运行这些代码需要较新版本的Ruby（最好是可本地编译的主分支）、Rust和C编译器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby中的Ractor模型及其在并发编程中的应用和挑战

不同观点：
• t-writescode认为Ractor模型中的邮箱和单线程操作队列可以解决很多并发压力问题，但对Ractor是否已经完全解决了邮箱的安全性问题表示不确定。他还提到对Rust在以Ruby为主题的文章中频繁出现感到不解，并表达了对演员模型（actor model）的偏好，认为Ractor被强制适应不合适的范式令人沮丧。

• dpflan引用了Mike Perham的工作，指出Ractor在实际应用中（如Sidekiq的扩展）面临编程困难，特别是由于Ractor不允许词法作用域或闭包变量访问。他认为Ractor编程需要新的代码模式，并将其难度与学习Golang的goroutines和channels相比较。

• kodablah分享了他们在项目中尝试使用Ractor的经历，但由于Google Protobuf库不支持Ractor安全，导致无法在Ractor中使用该库，最终放弃了使用Ractor。

• rco8786对文章表示赞赏，并认为创建一个生产就绪的Ractor安全数据结构库将大大推动Ractor的采用，解决当前的一个重大障碍。

补充讨论：
• 关于Ractor编程中的具体技术挑战，包括变量访问和代码模式的缺乏，是讨论中的一个重要方面。
• Ractor模型与其它并发模型的比较，如Golang的goroutines，也是讨论的一个焦点，显示出对不同编程范式的偏好和适应难度。
• Ractor在实际项目应用中的局限性，如对某些库的不兼容问题，是另一个值得注意的讨论点，这影响了Ractor的广泛采用。

data.title: Sell yourself, sell your work
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 文章强调，仅仅完成出色的工作并不足够，还需要主动宣传和分享，才能让世界受益并实现个人价值的最大化。作者指出，许多人虽然技术出色，但不愿意花时间撰写报告或分享成果，导致他们的工作无法被外界了解。因此，为了让他人知道并利用你的工作成果，必须克服对“宣传”的抵触心理，积极传播自己的成就。简而言之，做好工作后，还需要有效地“推销”自己和自己的工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该公开和宣传自己的项目和作品，以及这样做是否是实现作品和个人价值的前提。

不同观点：
• **支持公开和宣传**：Simonw 认为，记录和分享项目非常重要，尤其是通过博客或GitHub，这样不仅能防止项目过时，还能让更多人受益。他还提到自己后悔没有记录早期项目。Gyello 也分享了自己通过为亲友创建项目并展示这些项目所获得的满足感，尽管这些项目没有公开发布。

• **反对强制公开**：Henchman21 和 Iaaan 持反对意见，认为不是所有作品都必须公开或商业化才能体现其价值。Iaaan 强调，人们有权选择是否分享自己的创作，而不应被外界压力左右。Henchman21 进一步指出，作品的价值不一定在于商业化，人类努力的价值超越金钱。

• **强调内在价值**：Sashank_1509 引用了Albert Jay Nock的《Isiah’s Job》一文，认为真正卓越的工作不需要通过宣传来体现其价值，时间会证明其意义。Bravetraveler 和 Ryandrake 也认为，可靠性和个人的内在满足感比宣传更为重要，做好工作自然会有人关注。

• **中立或实用主义**：Boznz 和 Stocknoob 持中立态度，认为宣传与否取决于个人喜好和需求。Boznz 提到自己不擅长营销，但意识到记录和分享项目可能带来机会。Stocknoob 建议年轻程序员专注于自己的兴趣，而不是自我宣传，除非他们喜欢这样做。

补充讨论：
• **个人品牌和商业化**：Webprofusion 和 Rednafi 提到公开项目和写作有助于建立个人品牌，可能会带来职业机会。然而，Rednafi 也警告不要过度销售，否则可能适得其反。

• **批判商业化压力**：Bjornsing 指出，人们往往忽视了从他人工作中筛选出有价值的部分，而不是被营销牵着走。Maxlin 则用比喻说明，人类生活的意义在于自我满足，而非对外展示。

争议焦点：作品的价值是否需要通过公开和商业化来体现，以及是否应由外界压力决定个人是否应该分享自己的创作。

43476249.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该公开和宣传自己的项目和作品，以及这样做是否是实现作品和个人价值的前提。

不同观点：
• **支持公开和宣传**：Simonw 认为，记录和分享项目非常重要，尤其是通过博客或GitHub，这样不仅能防止项目过时，还能让更多人受益。他还提到自己后悔没有记录早期项目。Gyello 也分享了自己通过为亲友创建项目并展示这些项目所获得的满足感，尽管这些项目没有公开发布。

• **反对强制公开**：Henchman21 和 Iaaan 持反对意见，认为不是所有作品都必须公开或商业化才能体现其价值。Iaaan 强调，人们有权选择是否分享自己的创作，而不应被外界压力左右。Henchman21 进一步指出，作品的价值不一定在于商业化，人类努力的价值超越金钱。

• **强调内在价值**：Sashank_1509 引用了Albert Jay Nock的《Isiah’s Job》一文，认为真正卓越的工作不需要通过宣传来体现其价值，时间会证明其意义。Bravetraveler 和 Ryandrake 也认为，可靠性和个人的内在满足感比宣传更为重要，做好工作自然会有人关注。

• **中立或实用主义**：Boznz 和 Stocknoob 持中立态度，认为宣传与否取决于个人喜好和需求。Boznz 提到自己不擅长营销，但意识到记录和分享项目可能带来机会。Stocknoob 建议年轻程序员专注于自己的兴趣，而不是自我宣传，除非他们喜欢这样做。

补充讨论：
• **个人品牌和商业化**：Webprofusion 和 Rednafi 提到公开项目和写作有助于建立个人品牌，可能会带来职业机会。然而，Rednafi 也警告不要过度销售，否则可能适得其反。

• **批判商业化压力**：Bjornsing 指出，人们往往忽视了从他人工作中筛选出有价值的部分，而不是被营销牵着走。Maxlin 则用比喻说明，人类生活的意义在于自我满足，而非对外展示。

争议焦点：作品的价值是否需要通过公开和商业化来体现，以及是否应由外界压力决定个人是否应该分享自己的创作。

data.title: Devs say AI crawlers dominate traffic, forcing blocks on entire countries
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary:
软件开发者Xe Iaso遭遇亚马逊的AI爬虫流量攻击，导致其Git服务频繁不稳定和停机。尽管采取了多种防御措施，爬虫仍通过伪造用户代理和使用住宅IP代理绕过限制。Iaso最终创建了名为"Anubis"的系统，要求浏览器在访问前解决计算谜题，以此阻挡爬虫。然而，这种方法也给合法用户带来了延迟问题。

这一问题在开源社区广泛存在，许多项目的基础设施因AI爬虫而过载，导致服务不稳定和带宽成本上升。例如，Fedora Pagure项目不得不屏蔽巴西的所有流量，GNOME GitLab则采用了类似Anubis的系统，结果显示大部分请求是自动化的。

开源项目通常资源有限，面对AI爬虫的侵扰，维护者们感到负担沉重。例如，Inkscape项目的Martin Owens提到，他们的问题不仅来自传统的DDoS攻击，还包括一些公司无视规则、伪造浏览器信息。

社区对AI公司占用大量资源的行为感到不满，认为这些公司不尊重公共资源，且对受影响项目的诉求反应迟钝。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• **公司应采取更协作的方式进行数据抓取**：tedunangst认为，公司应该采取更协作的方式，比如限速数据抓取，以免压垮目标网站。如果目标网站在抓取后下线，那反而是“功能”。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击现象**：Nckpz分享了自己新项目在24小时内遭到大量垃圾表单提交攻击的经历，尽管没有对外宣传，但机器人迅速攻击了服务器。
• **激进的AI机器人对内容网站的影响**：ipaddr提到，由于激进的AI机器人，他们不得不关闭多个内容网站，这些机器人无视robots文件，导致服务器宕机。
• **特定AI机器人造成的DoS攻击**：rco8786描述了由Anthropic的ClaudeBot引发的DoS攻击，导致网站带宽超限，必须手动处理。

补充讨论：
• **反机器人措施的有效性与浏览器垄断问题**：userbinator指出，复杂的JS反机器人措施可能加剧浏览器垄断，建议使用简单HTML表单提问，以防止LLM（大型语言模型）破解。
• **对机器人检测和应对策略的建议**：edoloughlin提出了一种调皮的策略，即检测到AI机器人时，向其提供随机数据，让它们也感受到痛苦。
• **开源许可证的更新需求**：ANarrativeApe质疑是否需要根据当前机器人滥用行为更新开源许可证，以使这种滥用行为公开化。
• **创建私有网络的讨论**：haswell考虑创建一个类似“亲友”的私有网络，以重获发布信息的自由。
• **国家封锁和爬虫监管**：ggm认为，国家封锁是懒惰且不实用的，爬虫应该支付“愚蠢税”或被监管。
• **对不同类型网站的影响**：grotorea质疑这种现象是否仅影响非营利网站，并担心更严格的登录墙会导致网络内容向深层网络迁移。

争议焦点：
• **如何有效管理机器人流量和数据抓取行为**，包括技术手段（如反机器人措施）和政策手段（如爬虫监管、许可证更新）。
• **机器人流量的快速攻击和DoS攻击的普遍性及其对不同类型网站的影响**。

Software developer Xe Iaso
reached a breaking point
earlier this year when aggressive AI crawler traffic from Amazon overwhelmed their Git repository service, repeatedly causing instability and downtime. Despite configuring standard defensive measures—adjusting robots.txt, blocking known crawler user-agents, and filtering suspicious traffic—Iaso found that AI crawlers continued evading all attempts to stop them, spoofing user-agents and cycling through residential IP addresses as proxies.
Desperate for a solution, Iaso eventually resorted to moving their server behind a VPN and creating "Anubis," a custom-built proof-of-work challenge system that forces web browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing the site. "It's futile to block AI crawler bots because they lie, change their user agent, use residential IP addresses as proxies, and more," Iaso wrote in a
blog post
titled "a desperate cry for help." "I don't want to have to close off my Gitea server to the public, but I will if I have to."
Iaso's story highlights a broader crisis rapidly spreading across the open source community, as what appear to be aggressive AI crawlers increasingly overload community-maintained infrastructure, causing what amounts to persistent distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on vital public resources. According to a
comprehensive recent report
from LibreNews, some open source projects now see as much as 97 percent of their traffic originating from AI companies' bots, dramatically increasing bandwidth costs, service instability, and burdening already stretched-thin maintainers.
Kevin Fenzi, a member of the Fedora Pagure project's sysadmin team,
reported on his blog
that the project had to block all traffic from Brazil after repeated attempts to mitigate bot traffic failed. GNOME GitLab implemented Iaso's "Anubis" system, requiring browsers to solve computational puzzles before accessing content. GNOME sysadmin Bart Piotrowski
shared
on Mastodon that only about 3.2 percent of requests (2,690 out of 84,056) passed their challenge system, suggesting the vast majority of traffic was automated. KDE's GitLab infrastructure was temporarily knocked offline by crawler traffic originating from Alibaba IP ranges, according to LibreNews, citing a KDE Development chat.
While Anubis has proven effective at filtering out bot traffic, it comes with drawbacks for legitimate users. When many people access the same link simultaneously—such as when a GitLab link is shared in a chat room—site visitors can face significant delays. Some mobile users have reported waiting up to two minutes for the proof-of-work challenge to complete, according to the news outlet.
The situation isn't exactly new. In December, Dennis Schubert, who maintains infrastructure for the Diaspora social network,
described
the situation as "literally a DDoS on the entire internet" after discovering that AI companies accounted for 70 percent of all web requests to their services.
The costs are both technical and financial. The Read the Docs project reported that blocking AI crawlers immediately decreased their traffic by 75 percent, going from 800GB per day to 200GB per day. This change saved the project approximately $1,500 per month in bandwidth costs, according to their blog post "AI crawlers need to be more respectful."
A disproportionate burden on open source
The situation has created a tough challenge for open source projects, which rely on public collaboration and typically operate with limited resources compared to commercial entities. Many maintainers have reported that AI crawlers deliberately circumvent standard blocking measures, ignoring robots.txt directives, spoofing user agents, and rotating IP addresses to avoid detection.
As LibreNews reported, Martin Owens from the Inkscape project
noted
on Mastodon that their problems weren't just from "the usual Chinese DDoS from last year, but from a pile of companies that started ignoring our spider conf and started spoofing their browser info." Owens added, "I now have a prodigious block list. If you happen to work for a big company doing AI, you may not get our website anymore."
On Hacker News, commenters in threads
about the LibreNews
post last week and a
post on Iaso's battles
in January expressed deep frustration with what they view as AI companies' predatory behavior toward open source infrastructure. While these comments come from forum posts rather than official statements, they represent a common sentiment among developers.
As one Hacker News user
put it
, AI firms are operating from a position that "goodwill is irrelevant" with their "$100bn pile of capital." The discussions depict a battle between smaller AI startups that have worked collaboratively with affected projects and larger corporations that have been unresponsive despite allegedly forcing thousan

data.title: Better Shell History Search
data.author: ltratt
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过改进Unix终端中的命令历史搜索功能来提高工作效率。作者指出，许多人由于不熟悉快捷操作而浪费时间在重复输入命令上。虽然Bash等壳允许使用Ctrl-r进行子字符串搜索，但这种方法较为局限。作者推荐结合使用Ctrl-r和工具fzf，实现模糊搜索并同时显示多个匹配结果，大大提升了查找命令的速度和准确性。作者亲身体验表明，这一组合显著提高了其工作效率，并促使他更大胆地使用复杂命令。最后，作者还提到发现了另一个工具skim，相比fzf更符合其需求。尽管如此，作者认为无论选择哪个工具，都能显著提升Unix用户的效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： shell历史搜索工具的比较与改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持Atuin的多设备同步功能**：[jakebasile]认为Atuin非常有价值，尤其是在多台设备上使用时，可以保持历史记录同步，还可以按主机或目录进行筛选。
• **推荐zsh插件**：[northisup]建议使用zsh的zle插件，如history-search-multi-word和fast-syntax-highlighting，认为这些插件提供了良好的性能和语法高亮功能。
• **McFly的智能搜索**：[devjam]推荐McFly，它可以根据工作目录和最近执行的命令进行智能搜索和实时优先级排序。
• **fzf与bash自动补全的整合需求**：[worldsayshi]希望fzf能与bash自动补全整合，以获得更像代码补全的体验，并提到fzf-tab可能是一个解决方案，但仅适用于zsh。
• **对功能过载的担忧**：[fsckboy]担心新功能会打破原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖，并提到Linux中的一些功能逐渐消失，如中键粘贴。
• **Atuin与fzf/skim的比较**：[3r7j6qzi9jvnve]认为Atuin的模糊匹配不如fzf/skim，更倾向于使用skim的shell整合功能。
• **推荐hstr**：[bramgn]推荐hstr，认为这是一个很好的历史搜索工具，尽管自己没有广泛使用其他工具。
• **zsh-histdb的优点**：[Hobadee]使用zsh-histdb，并赞赏它显示返回状态和执行命令的目录功能。
• **Atuin的网络安全问题**：[joshka]解释Atuin的网络功能可以完全编译出来，并且历史记录是端到端加密的，认为其安全性足够好。

补充讨论：
• **共享历史记录的价值**：[larusso]认为共享历史记录在不同窗口/标签之间很重要，但对一些人来说可能存在争议，尤其是当重复执行某些命令时。
• **改进历史记录的功能建议**：[wodenokoto]希望历史记录能显示命令执行的位置、是否失败以及添加常用命令/收藏。
• **Bacon替代重复命令执行**：[joshka]提到Bacon可以替代重复执行的命令，如cargo test。
• **对新手的批评**：[SrslyJosh]批评不熟悉基础shell命令的人，并建议学习bash/zsh/sh以及基本工具如grep、sed、awk等。

争议焦点：
• **新功能与用户习惯的冲突**：一些用户（如[fsckboy]）担心新功能会破坏原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖。
• **工具的选择与偏好**：不同用户对工具的偏好不同，如Atuin、fzf、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，各有优缺点。

总结：
评论主要围绕shell历史搜索工具的功能、改进建议以及用户习惯的冲突展开。不同用户根据自己的需求和偏好推荐了不同的工具，如Atuin、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，并提出了一些功能改进建议，如整合fzf与bash自动补全、显示命令执行位置和是否失败等。同时，也有用户对新功能与原有用户习惯的冲突表示担忧。

I spend an awful lot of my day in Unix terminals running shell commands. For
some reason, the variance in efficiency between different people when using the shell
is huge: I know people who can run rings around me, and Iâve come across
more than one paid professional who doesnât use the âupâ key to retrieve the
previous command.
I chose that last example very deliberately: most of the commands most of us
run in the shell are highly repetitive. I typically run around 50-100 unique
(i.e. syntactically distinct) shell commands per working day
[1]
â but
Iâll often run a tiny subset of those commands (e.g.
cargo test
) hundreds of
time in a single day.
Since many command-line tools have hard-to-remember options, we can save huge
chunks of time â not to mention make fewer errors â if we can search our
shell history to find a previous incantation of a command we want to run. In
this post Iâm going to show how, with little effort, searching shell
history can look like this:
[Video]
Searching shell history
Larger Unix shells such as Bash have long allowed users to search through their
shell history by pressing
Ctrl-r
and entering a substring. If I (in order)
executed the commands
cat /etc/motd
then
cat /etc/rc.conf
, then
Ctrl-r
followed by âcatâ will first match
cat /etc/rc.conf
; pressing
Ctrl-r
again
will cycle backwards for the next match which is
cat /etc/motd
. I almost
never used this feature, because substring matching is too crude.
For example, I may know the command I want is
cat
, the leaf
name Iâm looking for is
motd
but I donât remember the directory: substring
matching canât help me find what Iâm looking for. Instead, I regularly used
grep
(with wildcards) to search through my shellâs history file instead.
For me, the game changer was pairing
Ctrl-r
with
fzf
, which brought two changes. First,
matching is âfuzzyâ, so I can type âc moâ and
cat /etc/motd
will be
matched. Second, multiple matches are shown at once. Typing âcatâ will show
me several
cat
commands, allowing me to quickly select the right
incantation (which may not have been the most recent).
Itâs difficult for me to overstate how powerful a feature this is. Few things
in life make me as happy as pressing
ctrl-R
then typing â
l1
â and having a 100
character command-line execution that runs a complicated debugging tool, with
multiple environment variables set, whose output gets put in
/tmp/l1
appear
in my terminal.
Using
Ctrl-r
and fzf roughly doubled my efficiency in the shell
overnight. Interestingly, it had an even greater long term effect: I became a
more ambitious user of shell commands because I knew I could outsource my
memory to fzf. For example, since itâs now very easy to recall past commands, I
no longer set global environment variables, which had previously caused me
grief when I forgot about them
[2]
. Now I set environment variables on a
per-command basis, knowing that I can recall them with
Ctrl-r
and fzf.
For many years my favoured shell was zsh. When I later moved from zsh to fish,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was the first thing I configured; and when I moved back to zsh
[3]
, and redid my configuration from scratch,
Ctrl-r
and fzf was again the first
thing I got working (shortly followed by
autosuggestions
). If you
take nothing else from this
post than â
Ctrl-r
and fzf are a significant productivity boon for Unix
usersâ, then I will have done something useful.
No tool, of course, is perfect. A
couple of months back I somehow stumbled across
skim
, an fzf-alike that out-of-the-box
happens to suit me just a little bit better than fzf. The differences
are mostly minor, and you wonât go far wrong with either tool. That said,
I find that skimâs matching more often finds the commands I want quickly,
I prefer skimâs UI, and I find it easier to install skim on
random boxes â small advantages, perhaps, but enough for switching to be
worth it for me.
Doing even better
Finding Skim encouraged me to quickly look around to see what else in this sphere might
improve my productivity. I quickly came across
Atuin
, which is a much
more sophisticated shell history recording mechanism: the video on its front
page showed a much nicer matching UI than I had previously considered possible.
However, I quickly realised Atuin wasnât for me or, at least, wasnât easily for
me.
43476793.article_summary: 本文讨论了如何通过改进Unix终端中的命令历史搜索功能来提高工作效率。作者指出，许多人由于不熟悉快捷操作而浪费时间在重复输入命令上。虽然Bash等壳允许使用Ctrl-r进行子字符串搜索，但这种方法较为局限。作者推荐结合使用Ctrl-r和工具fzf，实现模糊搜索并同时显示多个匹配结果，大大提升了查找命令的速度和准确性。作者亲身体验表明，这一组合显著提高了其工作效率，并促使他更大胆地使用复杂命令。最后，作者还提到发现了另一个工具skim，相比fzf更符合其需求。尽管如此，作者认为无论选择哪个工具，都能显著提升Unix用户的效率。
43476793.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： shell历史搜索工具的比较与改进建议

不同观点：
• **支持Atuin的多设备同步功能**：[jakebasile]认为Atuin非常有价值，尤其是在多台设备上使用时，可以保持历史记录同步，还可以按主机或目录进行筛选。
• **推荐zsh插件**：[northisup]建议使用zsh的zle插件，如history-search-multi-word和fast-syntax-highlighting，认为这些插件提供了良好的性能和语法高亮功能。
• **McFly的智能搜索**：[devjam]推荐McFly，它可以根据工作目录和最近执行的命令进行智能搜索和实时优先级排序。
• **fzf与bash自动补全的整合需求**：[worldsayshi]希望fzf能与bash自动补全整合，以获得更像代码补全的体验，并提到fzf-tab可能是一个解决方案，但仅适用于zsh。
• **对功能过载的担忧**：[fsckboy]担心新功能会打破原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖，并提到Linux中的一些功能逐渐消失，如中键粘贴。
• **Atuin与fzf/skim的比较**：[3r7j6qzi9jvnve]认为Atuin的模糊匹配不如fzf/skim，更倾向于使用skim的shell整合功能。
• **推荐hstr**：[bramgn]推荐hstr，认为这是一个很好的历史搜索工具，尽管自己没有广泛使用其他工具。
• **zsh-histdb的优点**：[Hobadee]使用zsh-histdb，并赞赏它显示返回状态和执行命令的目录功能。
• **Atuin的网络安全问题**：[joshka]解释Atuin的网络功能可以完全编译出来，并且历史记录是端到端加密的，认为其安全性足够好。

补充讨论：
• **共享历史记录的价值**：[larusso]认为共享历史记录在不同窗口/标签之间很重要，但对一些人来说可能存在争议，尤其是当重复执行某些命令时。
• **改进历史记录的功能建议**：[wodenokoto]希望历史记录能显示命令执行的位置、是否失败以及添加常用命令/收藏。
• **Bacon替代重复命令执行**：[joshka]提到Bacon可以替代重复执行的命令，如cargo test。
• **对新手的批评**：[SrslyJosh]批评不熟悉基础shell命令的人，并建议学习bash/zsh/sh以及基本工具如grep、sed、awk等。

争议焦点：
• **新功能与用户习惯的冲突**：一些用户（如[fsckboy]）担心新功能会破坏原有的用户习惯，尤其是对Emacs快捷键的依赖。
• **工具的选择与偏好**：不同用户对工具的偏好不同，如Atuin、fzf、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，各有优缺点。

总结：
评论主要围绕shell历史搜索工具的功能、改进建议以及用户习惯的冲突展开。不同用户根据自己的需求和偏好推荐了不同的工具，如Atuin、zsh插件、McFly和hstr，并提出了一些功能改进建议，如整合fzf与bash自动补全、显示命令执行位置和是否失败等。同时，也有用户对新功能与原有用户习惯的冲突表示担忧。

data.title: Show HN: A website for sharing the "Good, Bad, and Why"s of urban spaces
data.author: kappasan
data.article_summary: 《Community Atlas of Urban Phenomena》是一个让用户分享和标记城市中各种现象的平台，用户可以根据体验将现象标记为"Good"（好）、"Bad"（坏）、"Why"（为什么）等标签，并添加评论和照片。内容涵盖设计、艺术、文化、交通、基础设施、技术、安全、健康、自然、环境、商业等多个方面。用户发布的帖子示例包括对特别建筑、城市设施、交通问题等的评价，如"1000日元卡住了"、"イベント会場へのナビゲーション"（活动会场的导航）、"マンホール周りの印"（井盖周围的标记）等。平台还提供按地区、时间、标签等筛选功能，但存在一些功能不完善的问题，如评论功能不稳定，开发者承诺在下一版本中改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对网站功能的反馈及潜在应用

不同观点：
• upghost：对iOS的高亮和"翻译"功能改进表示赞赏，并感谢kappasan的分享。这表明该用户对技术改进的积极反馈。

• ripley12：对分享表示感谢，并表示有兴趣为网站添加温哥华的相关内容。这显示了用户对内容贡献的开放态度和参与意愿。

• bythreads：称赞网站的简洁性，并提到AI机器人会喜欢抓取此类信息。这反映了对网站设计简单和数据价值的认可，同时暗示了该网站可能被自动化程序利用的潜力。

• kappasan：作为原始分享者（OP），提供了有关注册表单的额外信息，指出使用非工作邮箱地址可以作为用户ID，但提醒用户如果忘记密码将无法重置。这揭示了网站注册流程中的一个潜在问题。

• mc3301：表示有很多日本的相关内容可以添加，显示出对内容贡献的兴趣和潜力。

• riffic：将网站与"模式语言"（Pattern Language）概念进行类比，表达了对网站能在其周边地区流行的期望。这提供了一个独特的视角，将网站功能与已有的学术概念联系起来。

补充讨论：
• 网站的用户注册流程存在一定的不便，尤其是密码重置问题。
• 用户对内容贡献表现出较高的积极性，尤其是对特定地域信息的添加。
• 有人关注到网站可能被自动化程序利用的潜力，这可能涉及数据安全和隐私问题。
• 一位用户将网站功能与"模式语言"联系起来，提供了一个理论上的比较，这可能为网站的应用和理解提供了新的视角。

data.author: mdp2021
data.article_summary: Simon Willison创建了一个GitHub Actions和GitHub Pages的Atom订阅源，用于抓取Ollama的最新模型数据。由于Ollama是笔记本电脑上运行模型的简便方式，新模型发布值得关注。他通过将示例HTML粘贴到Claude中，并请求生成一个Python脚本以转换为Atom格式，从而构建了该抓取工具。文章还提供了他们一起编写的脚本链接，并提及了一些近期其他文章。发布时间为2025年3月22日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RSS/Atom  feed 的优化建议以及对大语言模型（LLM）能力评估的讨论

不同观点：
• **RSS/Atom feed 条目数量问题**：[mdp2021] 认为目前的 RSS/Atom feed 条目数量过多（超过160条），建议缩短时间窗口，将条目数量减少到10条左右，以提高更新效率。同时，提出可以提供一个“完整版”的XML用于首次下载，之后用“精简版”进行日常更新。
  
• **"pulls" 值的无意义**：[mdp2021] 指出在 "proper" RSS feed 中，"pulls" 值没有实际意义，属于冗余或误导性信息，应予以修正。

• **对大语言模型能力评估的兴趣**：[mdp2021] 对 Simon 使用 Claude 构建网页抓取工具表示好奇，并提出是否有人维护一个对各 LLM 能力进行基准测试或非正式评估（如轶事或经验性）的列表，以帮助了解各模型的强项和弱项。

补充讨论：
• **对 Claude 的使用案例**：[mdp2021] 特别提到 Simon 选择使用 Claude 构建特定任务的工具，暗示了对不同 LLM 模型在实际应用中表现的关注和潜在比较兴趣。

• **技术细节的关注**：[mdp2021] 对 feed 条目数量和 "pulls" 值的关注显示出对技术细节的重视，希望通过优化这些细节提升使用体验。

争议焦点：
• 当前 RSS/Atom feed 的条目数量和更新频率是否合理，是否有必要提供两种版本的 feed 以平衡用户需求和系统负载。

data.title: Saying 'pandemic is over,' NIH institute starts cutting Covid-19 research
data.author: thenerdhead
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新冠病毒是否仍然具有较大影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：新冠病毒依然具有严重影响。WorldPeas分享了自己的经历，表示自己再次感染了新冠，并且症状和第一次感染时一样严重。这表明至少对某些个体而言，新冠病毒的威胁依然存在，并非已经完全无害。
• 观点二：未明确表述但可推断出的潜在反对意见可能是，新冠病毒对大部分人来说已经不再像以前那么严重，可能有人认为随着疫苗和群体免疫，病毒的危害已经减弱。然而，WorldPeas的个人经历提供了反例，显示出病毒仍可能对某些人造成严重影响。

补充讨论：
• WorldPeas强调自己的经历是个人案例（n=1），说明他意识到单个个例不能代表整体情况，但他的分享仍然指出了新冠病毒在某些情况下仍可能具有严重影响。
• 评论中提到“anecdotal”（轶事性），表明作者承认这仅是个别现象，可能不具备广泛的统计意义，但这种个人经历在讨论中依然具有价值，尤其是在讨论公共健康问题时。

data.article_summary: 本文介绍了与YouTube相关的多项信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者信息、广告、开发者合作、条款规定、隐私政策、安全指南以及YouTube的使用方式和全新功能测试。此外，还提到NFL Sunday Ticket的服务。文章末尾注明版权为2025年Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：使用Ghidra中的代码片段通过LLM（如ChatGPT）自动分析的可行性和效果

不同观点：
• [负面经验] brokensegue分享了自己的负面经验，表示直接从Ghidra复制粘贴代码到LLM并希望获得有效分析的结果并不成功。这暗示了当前的LLM在处理复杂逆向工程任务时可能存在局限性。

• [潜在价值] 尽管brokensegue的个人体验不佳，他们仍然认为为这类任务建立基准测试（benchmarks）会很有价值，暗示出对未来改进和标准化评估的期望，可能认为通过系统化的测试可以找到LLM在逆向工程中的最佳应用方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：当前LLM在处理逆向工程任务（如Ghidra代码分析）时的有效性存在争议。虽然有人可能认为LLM能提升工作效率，但实际效果因任务复杂性和模型能力而异。

• 论据和例子：实际案例中，直接复制粘贴代码到LLM未能成功解析，表明在逆向工程领域，LLM可能需要更针对性的训练或更高的专业性。

• 未来展望：提到建立benchmarks的需求，表明了对未来LLM在逆向工程中应用的积极预期，希望通过标准化评估来提升其实用性。

data.title: Why Did the Government Declare War on My Adorable Tiny Truck?
data.author: adebiase44
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型车辆（如SUV、皮卡）与小型车辆（如Kei卡车、摩托车）在道路安全上的对比，以及驾驶行为与车辆自动化对驾驶安全的影响。

不同观点：
• AlexJPlant认为，当前美国乘客车辆越来越多地被SUV和皮卡所主导，这些车辆比以前的车型更大更重，对其他道路使用者（尤其是行人）更致命。消费者为了自身安全购买这些车辆，但实际上增加了对其他道路使用者的危险。他还提到Kei卡车有相反的问题：对其他道路使用者无害，但对驾驶者和乘客而言，遇到大型车辆时更危险。他将这种情况类比为摩托车，指出人们常认为摩托车危险，但忽视了统计数据中的偏差和其他司机的不专心。他还指出，随着车辆变得更大、更舒适和自动化，人们逐渐忽视了驾驶的实际风险，将驾驶体验等同于在客厅中放松。

• BMc2020没有直接发表观点，但通过提供一个存档链接，可能意在为讨论提供更多背景信息或数据支持。

• Slackfan没有直接参与关于车辆安全的讨论，而是以讽刺的语气提到马萨诸塞州的官僚体系问题，可能意在表达对当地行政效率的不满，而非直接回应有关车辆安全的主帖内容。

补充讨论：
• AlexJPlant进一步讨论了驾驶文化的变化，指出驾驶行为的价值在几十年来逐渐被贬低，人们在驾驶时注意力转移到其他事情上，加之车辆自动化和舒适性的提升，使得人们忽视了驾驶的潜在危险。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于大型车辆的普及对道路安全的负面影响，以及人们在选择车辆时如何平衡自身安全与公共安全的责任。此外，驾驶自动化和舒适性提升是否导致人们忽视驾驶风险也是讨论的一个焦点。

data.title: Chewing gum can shed microplastics into saliva, pilot study finds
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 一项初步研究发现，嚼口香糖可能会将数百至数千个微塑料颗粒释放到唾液中并被摄入。美国化学学会（ACS）2025年春季会议上发表的这项研究显示，无论是天然还是合成口香糖，都会在咀嚼过程中释放微塑料。研究测试了五种合成口香糖和五种天然口香糖，结果发现每克口香糖平均释放约100个微塑料，有些甚至高达600个。一个大的口香糖可能释放多达3000个塑料颗粒。如果按每人每年嚼160至180根口香糖计算，可能摄入约30,000个微塑料。研究还发现，微塑料主要在前两分钟内脱落，且天然和合成口香糖的释放量相似，均含有聚烯烃等塑料成分。研究人员强调，虽然尚未确定微塑料对人体的危害，但建议人们采取措施减少暴露。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：口香糖中塑料成分的来源、分类及其影响

不同观点：
• **[ricardobeat]** 对口香糖中“天然”成分的定义表示怀疑，质疑其中塑料的来源，是否是误标或欺诈行为。他希望了解这些塑料是如何被定义和归类的。

• **[xattt]** 关心塑料在口香糖中如何释放出来，并提出疑问：这些塑料碎片在再次咀嚼时是否会重新整合回口香糖中，进而影响其对环境或人体的影响。

• **[more-nitor]** 认为将所有塑料成分简单地标记为“微塑料”是不准确的。他指出不同的塑料种类（如聚乙烯、聚丙烯等）可能会有不同的化学性质和影响，应该区别对待，而不是一概而论。

• **[wkat4242]** 对现代口香糖含有塑料成分并不感到意外，指出由于天然成分成本过高，使用塑料替代是当今普遍的做法。他隐含了对市场因成本考虑而放弃天然成分的批评。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于口香糖中塑料成分的来源、分类和影响是否得到了充分解释和正确标记。
• 不同讨论者对于塑料在口香糖中的存在形式、对环境和健康的影响有不同的关注点，有人质疑标记的准确性，有人关心塑料的物理行为，还有人关注不同塑料种类的具体影响。
• 市场经济因素也被提及，天然成分因成本问题被塑料替代，反映了消费品行业中成本和质量之间的权衡。

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
Lea este comunicado de prensa en español
SAN DIEGO, March 25, 2025 — Plastic is everywhere. And many products we use in everyday life, such as
cutting boards
,
clothes
and
cleaning sponges
, can expose people to tiny, micrometer-wide plastic particles called microplastics. Now, chewing gum could be added to the list. In a pilot study, researchers found that chewing gum can release hundreds to thousands of microplastics per piece into saliva and potentially be ingested.
The researchers will present their results at the spring meeting of the American Chemical Society (ACS). ACS Spring 2025 is being held March 23-27; it features about 12,000 presentations on a range of science topics.
Both natural and synthetic chewing gums released microplastics into saliva in a pilot study.
New Africa/Shutterstock.com
“Our goal is not to alarm anybody,” says Sanjay Mohanty, the project’s principal investigator and an engineering professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA). “Scientists don’t know if microplastics are unsafe to us or not. There are no human trials. But we know we are exposed to plastics in everyday life, and that’s what we wanted to examine here.”
Animal studies and studies with human cells show that microplastics could cause harm, so while we wait for more definitive answers from the scientific community, individuals can take steps to reduce their exposure to microplastics.
Scientists estimate that humans consume tens of thousands of microplastics
(between 1 micrometer- and 5 millimeters-wide) every year through foods, drinks, plastic packaging, coatings, and production or manufacturing processes. Yet, chewing gum as a potential source of microplastics hasn’t been widely studied, despite the candy’s worldwide popularity. So, Mohanty and a graduate student in his lab, Lisa Lowe, wanted to identify how many microplastics a person could potentially ingest from chewing natural and synthetic gums.
Chewing gums are made from a rubbery base, sweetener, flavorings and other ingredients. Natural gum products use a plant-based polymer, such as chicle or other tree sap, to achieve the right chewiness, while other products use synthetic rubber bases from petroleum-based polymers.
“Our initial hypothesis was that the synthetic gums would have a lot more microplastics because the base is a type of plastic,” says Lowe, who started the project as an undergraduate intern at UCLA and the presenter of this research.
The researchers tested five brands of synthetic gum and five brands of natural gum, all of which are commercially available. Mohanty says they wanted to reduce the human factor of varied chewing patterns and saliva, so they had seven pieces from each brand all chewed by one person.
In the lab, the person chewed the piece of gum for 4 minutes, producing samples of saliva every 30 seconds, then a final mouth rinse with clean water, all of which got combined into a single sample. In another experiment, saliva samples were collected periodically over 20 minutes to look at the release rate of microplastics from each piece of gum. Then, the researchers measured the number of microplastics present in each saliva sample. Plastic particles were either stained red and counted under a microscope or analyzed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, which also provided the polymer composition.
Lowe measured an average of 100 microplastics released per gram of gum, though some individual gum pieces released as many as 600 microplastics per gram. A typical piece of gum weighs between 2 and 6 grams, meaning a large piece of gum could release up to 3,000 plastic particles. If the average person chews 160 to 180 small sticks of gum per year, the researchers estimated that could result in the ingestion of around 30,000 microplastics. If the average person consumes tens of thousands of microplastics per year, gum chewing could greatly increase the ingested amount.
“Surprisingly, both synthetic and natural gums had similar amounts of microplastics released when we chewed them,” says Lowe. And they also contained the same polymers: polyolefins, polyethylene terephthalates, polyacrylamides and polystyrenes. The most abundant polymers for both types of gum were polyolefins, a group of plastics that includes polyethylene and polypropylene.
Most of the microplastics detached from gum within the first 2 minutes of chewing. But Mohanty says they weren’t released because of enzymes in saliva breaking them down. Rather, the act of chewing is abrasive enough to make pieces flake off. And after 8 minutes of chewing, 94% of the plastic particles collected during the tests had been released. data.author: bumbledraven
data.article_summary: 文章《The Sad, Beautiful Fact That We're All Going To Miss Almost Everything》反思了我们作为文化消费者所面临的现实：由于文化作品（书籍、音乐、电影、电视、艺术等）数量庞大，任何人都不可能全部体验。即使每天努力阅读或观看，我们依然只能触及冰山一角。文章提出，面对这一事实，我们应学会“筛选”和“放弃”。“筛选”意味着选择值得花时间的作品，而“放弃”则是接受自己无法体验所有有价值的作品。作者强调，“博览群书”不是一个终点，而是一种持续的过程，我们应放下必须“全面掌握”的负担，享受我们能接触到的文化内容。

• 有些用户指出，过去的一些技术虽然在当时很流行，但并未经受住时间的考验，很快被遗忘或取代。他们对这些技术的历史影响持保留态度。

补充讨论：
• 有用户提到，某些技术之所以在当时流行，是因为它们解决了那个时代的特定问题或需求，而不一定是因为它们在技术上有多先进。
• 讨论中有人以具体例子（如 Commodore 64 和 Forth 语言）来说明过去流行技术的兴衰。这些例子用来支持不同观点，有的用来说明技术过时，有的则用来说明其历史价值。

43477379.article_content:
The Sad, Beautiful Fact That We're All Going To Miss Almost Everything
We take a moment to reflect on being "well-read," and on the fact that the smartest thing you can do as a consumer of culture is admit that you'll never know everything.
Opinion
The Sad, Beautiful Fact That We're All Going To Miss Almost Everything
April 18, 2011
9:55 AM ET
Linda Holmes
Enlarge this image
iStockphoto.com
iStockphoto.com
The vast majority of the world's books, music, films, television and art, you will never see. It's just numbers.
Consider books alone. Let's say you read two a week, and sometimes you take on a long one that takes you a
whole
week. That's quite a brisk pace for the average person. That lets you finish, let's say, 100 books a year. If we assume you start now, and you're 15, and you are willing to continue at this pace until you're 80. That's 6,500 books, which really sounds like a lot.
Let's do you another favor: Let's further assume you limit yourself to books from the last, say, 250 years. Nothing before 1761. This cuts out giant, enormous swaths of literature, of course, but we'll assume you're willing to write off thousands of years of writing in an effort to be reasonably well-read.
Sponsor Message
Of course, by the time you're 80, there will be 65 more years of new books, so by then, you're dealing with 315 years of books, which allows you to read about 20 books from each year. You'll have to break down your 20 books each year between fiction and nonfiction – you have to cover history, philosophy, essays, diaries, science, religion, science fiction, westerns, political theory ... I hope you weren't planning to go out very much.
You can hit the highlights, and you can specialize enough to become knowledgeable in some things, but most of what's out there, you'll have to ignore. (Don't forget books not written in English! Don't forget to learn all the other languages!)
Oh, and heaven help your kid, who will either have to throw out maybe 30 years of what you deemed most critical or be even more selective than you had to be.
We could do the same calculus with film or music or, increasingly, television – you simply have no chance of seeing even most of what exists. Statistically speaking, you will die having missed almost everything.
Roger Ebert recently wrote a
lovely piece
about the idea of being "well-read," and specifically about the way writers aren't read as much once they've been dead a long time. He worries – well, not worries, but laments a little – that he senses people don't read Henry James anymore, that they don't read Sinclair Lewis, that their knowledge of Allen Ginsberg is limited to
Howl
.
Sponsor Message
It's undoubtedly true; there are things that fade. But I can't help blaming, in part, the fact that we also simply have access to more and more things to choose from more and more easily. Netflix, Amazon, iTunes – you wouldn't have to go and search dusty used bookstores or know the guy who works at a record store in order to hear most of that stuff you're missing. You'd only have to choose to hear it.
You used to have a limited number of reasonably practical choices presented to you, based on what bookstores carried, what your local newspaper reviewed, or what you heard on the radio, or what was taught in college by a particular English department. There was a
huge
amount of selection that took place above the consumer level. (And here, I don't mean "consumer" in the crass sense of consumerism, but in the sense of one who devours, as you do a book or a film you love.)
Now, everything gets dropped into our laps, and there are really only two responses if you want to feel like you're well-read, or well-versed in music, or whatever the case may be: culling and surrender.
Culling is the choosing you do for yourself. It's the sorting of what's worth your time and what's not worth your time. It's saying, "I deem
Keeping Up With The Kardashians
a poor use of my time, and therefore, I choose not to watch it." It's saying, "I read the last Jonathan Franzen book and fell asleep six times, so I'm not going to read this one."
Surrender, on the other hand, is the realization that you do not have time for everything that would be worth the time you invested in it if you had the time, and that this fact doesn't have to threaten your sense that you are well-read. Surrender is the moment when you say, "I bet every single one of those 1,000 books I'm supposed to read before I die is very, very good, but I cannot read them all, and they will have to go on the list of things I didn't get to."
Sponsor Message
It is the recognition that well-read is not a destination; there is nowhere to get to, and if you assume there is somewhere to get to, you'd have to live a thousand years to even think about getting there, and by the time you got there, there would be a thousand years to catch up on.

data.article_summary: 弗朗茨·埃德尔曼奖（Franz Edelman Award）由运筹学与管理科学协会（INFORMS）每年颁发，旨在表彰在组织层面成功应用运筹学的卓越成就。该奖项始于1971年，原名TIMS奖，1982年为纪念运筹学家弗朗茨·埃德尔曼而更名。国际竞争包括来自工业、政府、医疗和非营利部门的六支团队，最终在INFORMS商业分析会议上宣布获胜者，并颁发10,000美元奖金。历年来，获奖项目的累计收益近2500亿美元。近期获奖者包括Molslinjen和Halfspace（2024年）、Walmart（2023年）以及智利政府部门（2022年）等。

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Edelman Award logo
The Franz Edelman Award for Achievement in Operations Research and the Management Sciences
recognizes excellence in the execution of
operations research
on the organizational level.
About
[
edit
]
The award is presented annually by the
Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences
(INFORMS).
The international competition pits six teams from industry, government, healthcare, and the non-profit sectors. The competition takes place at the INFORMS Business Analytics Conference and concludes with the announcement of the winner at a gala dinner at the conference. It began in 1971 as the TIMS Prize and was named for Franz Edelman, the operations research director of
RCA
, shortly after his death in 1982. It carries a cash award of $10,000. Since its inception, nearly $250 billion in benefits have been tabulated among Franz Edelman Award finalist teams. Following the competition, INFORMS publishes papers by the Edelman finalists in the January issue of the INFORMS journal
Interfaces

• [tmtvl] 对许可证兼容性提出质疑，询问在GitHub上使用何种许可证能够与所有其他许可证兼容。这暗示了对开源项目中许可证复杂性的关注，特别是当涉及多重许可证时可能产生的冲突。

• [mondov] 将讨论的工具与GitHub Copilot进行比较，质疑新工具相对于已有工具（如Copilot）的优势。这表明用户可能对工具的独特功能和改进点感兴趣，尤其是在已经有类似功能工具的情况下。

• [cocodill] 对要求通过GitHub登录的方式提出疑问，反映了一些用户对隐私和数据安全的关注，也可能涉及对不必要登录要求的抵触。

补充讨论：
- 许可证兼容性是一个关键的法律和技术问题，尤其在开源项目中，开发者需要确保他们的项目不会侵犯其他项目的版权或违反许可证协议。
- 用户对现有工具（如GitHub Copilot）的熟悉程度可能会影响他们对新工具的接受程度，因此新工具需要明确其相较于已有工具的独特优势。
- 登录和隐私问题在当今的数字环境中愈发重要，用户对额外的登录要求往往持有谨慎态度，尤其是当他们不确定该要求的必要性时。

data.title: Toyota's 'Circular Factory' Idea Could Be a Great Alternative to Junk Yards
data.author: zfg
data.article_summary: 丰田汽车通过其新启动的丰田循环工厂（TCF）项目，致力于减少报废车辆（ELVs）对环境的影响，并挖掘其经济价值。该项目将在欧盟市场首先实施，首家工厂位于英国的丰田汽车制造工厂。通过该项目，报废车辆将经过验证、拆解，其材料和零件将被分类用于再利用、再制造和回收。丰田计划每年回收10,000辆报废车辆，并将其中的120,000个零件重新销售，同时回收300吨高纯度塑料和8,200吨钢材等材料。该项目不仅旨在减少环境污染，还计划在全欧洲推广，并与其他组织合作推动循环经济和碳中和目标。相比美国的“旧车换现金”计划，丰田的举措更具可持续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对OEM厂商控制二手汽车零部件市场的担忧及其实际可行性

不同观点：
• [potato3732842的观点] 认为OEM厂商推动集中化处理二手汽车零部件的举措，是为了加强对市场的控制，目的是限制独立 junkyard 的存在。他们可能通过声称某些零件"不可修复"来拒绝销售，从而削弱二手市场。论据包括对OEM厂商垄断动机的怀疑和对市场自由流通的担忧。

• [calmbonsai的观点] 不同意potato3732842的看法，认为OEM厂商不可能实现这种控制。该评论指出，德国激励措施更高，且大众的类似计划已经失败。此外，现有的重型农用设备市场例子显示，OEM厂商垄断不会成功。该评论还指出，二手零件市场利润丰厚，OEM厂商垄断只会导致产品内置的报废策略和创新不足。

• [1970-01-01的观点] 提出一个实际问题，即汽车设计更新换代导致旧零件最终无法继续流通。他们认为，随着时间推移，旧零件的储存和分类将占用过多空间，超出junkyard的处理能力。这暗示了依赖二手零件市场的实际操作困难。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于OEM厂商是否能够成功控制或垄断二手零件市场，以及这种控制对市场自由和创新的潜在负面影响。
- 论据中提到了德国激励政策、大众的失败案例以及重型农用设备市场的现有情况，作为OEM厂商难以垄断二手市场的证据。
- 另一个值得注意的点是关于旧零件储存和处理的实际问题，这与市场运作的可行性相关联。

43476244.article_content:
Getty Images
With one junked car at a time, Toyota looks to reduce, reuse, and recycle its way into another profit stream while keeping trash out of well, actual streams. We’ve seen plenty of press releases describing sustainability and other green initiatives, but we have not seen many automakers talking about taking responsibility for its cars decades after they’re built. This could be an interesting idea.
The Toyota Circular Factory is a new initiative that will curate what they call end-of-life vehicles (ELVs—junkers bound for the bone yard) and piece them out for repurposing, remanufacturing, and recycling. ELVs are vehicles tagged as hazardous waste, usually due to age or as the result of a crash.
According to the
European Union
, more than six million vehicles are left to rot, causing not only environmental issues but also an economic loss in the millions for the materials that can be repurposed. As such, the EU ELV Directive went into effect in 2000, with a regulation update proposed in 2023. The directive sets minimum requirements, which can be adapted for each member country.
The TCF program was established by Toyota Motor Europe (TME) and its name refers to all of TME’s recycling activities within the EU market. Globally, it’s the first operation of its kind within Toyota. The first location will be at Toyota Motor Manufacturing UK (TMUK)’s Burnaston plant, whose principal build is the Toyota Corolla.
Toyota Motor Europe
Through the TCF, each ELV will go through an extensive validation process before being sorted. Materials and parts will be tagged for three key areas: reusability for resale, refurbishing, and recycling. Reusable parts will be sold through Toyota retailers and parts distributors. Raw materials like copper, aluminum, steel, and plastic would be recycled and used in the production of new parts. Everything will be assessed, including commodities like batteries and wheels, on where their second life will begin.
“We initially anticipate recycling around 10,000 vehicles a year in our UK facility, which will give new life to 120,000 parts, recover 300 tons of high purity plastic and 8,200 tons of steel—amongst other materials,” said Leon van der Merwe, Vice President of Circular Economy at Toyota Motor Europe.
He added, “As a next step for the Toyota Circular Factory concept, we plan to roll out similar operations across Europe. And we’re not stopping at our own facilities – we are eager to collaborate with other organisations who share our passion of circularity and commitment to carbon neutrality.”
How does TMUK obtain these ELVs anyway? Per the
UK’s ELV regulations
, vehicles are registered but automakers also need to provide a take-back program free of charge. And there is an “unlimited fine” for non-compliance with ELVs.
This sounds more purposeful and just a better overall plan than, say,
Cash for Clunkers
. That federal program was done purely as an economic stimulus that resulted in thousands of vehicles being destroyed. Whereas in Toyota’s eyes, end of life really means a second chance.

data.title: After DDoS attacks, Blizzard rolls back Hardcore WoW deaths
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary: 《魔兽世界》经典怀旧服的“硬核模式”以角色死亡永久删除为特色。过去，无论死亡原因，Blizzard都不允许恢复角色。然而，由于近期一系列针对硬核模式玩家的DDoS攻击导致大量角色死亡，Blizzard决定修改政策，将在“大规模事件且被认为影响游戏 integrity”时酌情恢复角色。这一变化源于知名公会OnlyFangs多次遭遇DDoS攻击，导致成员角色死亡，影响尤其严重。尽管Blizzard仍坚持一般死亡不恢复的政策，但此次针对恶意攻击做出了例外处理，以保护玩家体验。不过，攻击背后的恶意动机仍需更有效的服务器保护措施来防范。

World of Warcraft Classic
's Hardcore mode has set itself apart from the average MMO experience simply by
making character death permanent
across the entire in-game realm. For years, Blizzard has
not allowed any appeals or rollbacks
for these Hardcore mode character deaths, even when such deaths came as the direct result of a server disconnection or gameplay bug.
Now, Blizzard says it's modifying that policy somewhat in response to a series of "unprecedented distributed-denial-of-service (DDOS) attacks" undertaken "with the singular goal of disrupting players’ experiences." The
World of Warcraft
developer says it may now resurrect Classic Hardcore characters "at our sole discretion" when those deaths come "in a mass event which we deem inconsistent with the integrity of the game."
RIP OnlyFangs?
The high stakes inherent to
WoW
's Classic Hardcore mode have made it an appealing target for streamers and other online content creators looking to build an audience.
Dozens
of the most popular Hardcore
WoW
streamers have been gathering together as part of
the OnlyFangs Guild
, a group dedicated to the idea that "every decision matters and one mistake can mean the end of a character’s journey."
In recent weeks, though, many of those OnlyFangs characters' journeys have ended as the result of a
series
of
DDOS attacks
that impacted all of
World of Warcraft
and other Battle.net games. Those attacks seemed
suspiciously timed
to
coincide with major livestreamed OnlyFangs raids
and
negatively impacted many other players
in the process.
After weeks of OnlyFangs stream disruptions and character deaths from these server attacks, prominent guild member sodapoppin
posted on the guild Discord
that "I'd expect OnlyFangs is over... it's a terrible ending IMO, but that's the ending we got." In that same message, sodapoppin said it was clear that "the DDOS attacks are centered on us" and that he couldn't foresee asking guild members to continue streaming given the frequency and long-term consequences of those attacks.
"I don't feel comfortable dragging people through getting world buffs, flasks, and consumes etc., just to raid with the anxiety and probably the actuality of just being DDOS'd again and dying," sodapoppin wrote.
Blizzard to the rescue?
Sodapoppin allowed that OnlyFangs might continue "if we get a rollback [of the DDOS-related deaths] or I hear of some solid... DDOS protection" but added that they "don't see that happening." Last night, though, Blizzard surpassed sodapoppin's expectations and
changed its
Classic
Hardcore permadeath policy
to specifically deal with situations like this.
"Recently, we have experienced unprecedented distributed-denial-of-service (DDOS) attacks that impacted many Blizzard game services, including Hardcore realms, with the singular goal of disrupting players’ experiences,"
WoW Classic
Associate Production Director Clay Stone
wrote in a public message
. "As we continue our work to further strengthen the resilience of
WoW
realms and our rapid response time, we’re taking steps to resurrect player-characters that were lost as a result of these attacks."
While Blizzard's general policy on Hardcore mode deaths hasn't changed, Stone writes that the recent deaths due to DDOS are different because they "are an intentionally malicious effort made by third-party bad actors, and we believe the severity and results of DDOS attacks specifically warrant a different response."
That's not entirely out of step with Blizzard's
longstanding Hardcore Mode policies
, which specifically prohibit "deliberate action to hamper or significantly impede the ability of other players to enjoy the game" or "actions to deliberately cause the death of another player." But those policies were designed to punish various forms of in-game griefing, not for an anonymous botnet attacking the game servers themselves.
Now that DDOS-related deaths are no longer permanent, the griefers responsible for those attacks will hopefully have less motivation to take out all of Battle.net just to impact one
WoW
raid. But the appeal of disrupting specific scheduled streams will remain until Blizzard can find some way to protect its servers more effectively.

Top national security officials inadvertently added a journalist to a Signal group chat discussing plans for military strikes in Yemen.

Top national security officials inadvertently added a journalist to a Signal group chat discussing plans for military strikes in Yemen.

US national security
Pentagon warned staffers against using Signal before White House chat leak
Bulletin sent on 18 March said Russian hackers could access messages as Trump officials now downplay blunder
US politics live – latest updates
José Olivares
Tue 25 Mar 2025 15.19 EDT
Last modified on Tue 25 Mar 2025 15.43 EDT
Share
The Pentagon recently warned its employees against using Signal, the encrypted messaging app, due to a technical vulnerability, an
NPR
report reveals.
The report comes one day after the Atlantic published a story detailing how top
national security officials
, including the US vice-president and US defense secretary, had accidentally added a journalist to a Signal group chat, which revealed plans for military strikes in Yemen.
The Atlantic’s revelations sparked
widespread outrage at the security lapse
and sent ripples of shock at the breach through diplomatic circles across the world. However, Trump administration officials have tried to play down the sensitivity of the information exposed to the journalist.
But according to a Pentagon “OPSEC special bulletin” seen by NPR reporters and sent on 18 March, Russian hacking groups may exploit the vulnerability in Signal to spy on encrypted organizations, potentially targeting “persons of interest”.
Trump dismisses Signal security failure as ‘the only glitch in two months’
Read more
Signal uses end-to-end encryption for its messaging and calls. It is also an “open source” application, meaning the app’s code is open to independent review for any vulnerabilities. The app is typically used as a secure method to communicate.
The Pentagon-wide memo said “third party messaging apps” like Signal are permitted to be used to share unclassified information, but they are not allowed to be used to send “non-public” unclassified information.
In a statement to NPR, a spokesperson for Signal said they were “not aware of any vulnerabilities or supposed ones that we haven’t addressed publicly”.
The Atlantic’s story, in which the editor-in-chief, Jeffrey Goldberg, describes the Signal back-and-forth between senior
Trump administration
officials, led to widespread ridicule online, pointing to top officials’ lack of candor when discussing military strikes, and the original mistake in adding the journalist to the sensitive chat. The chat included top-level officials within the Trump administration, including the vice-president,
JD Vance
, the defense secretary,
Pete Hegseth
, the CIA director, John Ratcliffe, and others.
Goldberg did not release the entirety of the messages in the article. During an appearance on a liberal podcast on Tuesday, Goldberg said he refused to release the full thread, despite the Trump administration saying no classified information was shared. Trump
dismissed the security leak as a “glitch
”.

The US has been striking Houthi areas since November 2023, when, in retaliation for the US-backed Israeli attacks on Gaza, the Houthis began to target commercial and military vessels in the Red Sea.

data.title: An iPad dug up from the Thames solved museum thieves' murder plot
data.author: vinni2
data.article_summary: An iPad Mini found buried in the River Thames helped police uncover an international crime network involved in a murder plot. How an iPad dug up from the Thames solved museum thieves' murder plot
18 hours ago
Share
Save
Thomas Mackintosh
BBC News, London
Share
Save
Met Police
The iPad Mini was found buried one inch under the sand of the River Thames and linked to a near fatal shooting five-and-a-half years earlier
A Ming vase stolen from a Swiss museum. A shooting at a comedian's house in Woodford, east London. The robbery of a luxury apartment in Sevenoaks, Kent.
These seemingly unconnected events were all part of a web of international organised crime that police untangled after a six-year-long investigation.
A key piece of evidence - an iPad, found under an inch of sand on the foreshore of the River Thames just downstream from the O2 Arena.
Its discovery was pivotal to the investigation that has led to three people being found guilty at the Old Bailey of the near-assassination of one of Britain's most notorious armed robbers.
When found by a police officer with a metal detector on a cold November morning last year, the iPad was found caked in mud having been underwater for more than five years.
Forensics were able to clean it and open the Sim tray – which still contained a pink Vodafone Sim card.
Call data that was subsequently salvaged provided damning evidence on three men - Louis Ahearne, Stewart Ahearne and Daniel Kelly - who were all also involved in a heist at a museum in Switzerland a month earlier.
"I've questioned this a lot," Det Supt Matthew Webb ponders. "Is it calamitous blunders tripping them up or was it just they were so blasé they wouldn't get caught?"
A 'meticulously planned' assassination plot
Video doorbell footage captured audio of several gunshots
The Ahearne brothers and Kelly first caught the attention of police after gunshots pierced the silence of a late summer evening in an affluent Woodford area on 11 July 2019.
Six bullets tore through a glass conservatory at a luxury property owned by comedian Russell Kane that had been rented out to Paul Allen.
One severed one of Allen's fingers, the other went through his throat and became lodged in his spinal cord, leaving him struggling to breathe and bleeding profusely.
"He's been shot, he's been shot!" Allen's partner, Jade Bovington, screamed.
Met Police
Two bullets tore through the glass of a conservatory and hit Paul Allen as he stood inside his kitchen
As she frantically called an ambulance, neighbours and a private security guard heard the cries and rushed to render first aid.
One eyewitness described seeing an unidentified man vault a low wall, run between some bushes and get straight into a waiting vehicle which immediately sped off.
To this day, Allen relies on a wheelchair, paralysed below his upper chest.
Getty Images
Pictured in Morocco, Paul Allen was one of seven men who were jailed for their roles in the Securitas raid in February 2006
Allen gained notoriety as one of the ringleaders of what remains Britain's biggest ever armed robbery. In 2006, Allen was part of a balaclava-wearing gang toting guns including an AK-47 assault rifle who threatened to kill staff at the Securitas depot in Tonbridge, Kent. They
stole £53m in Bank of England cash notes
- leaving behind £154m which would not fit into their lorry.
Allen fled to Morocco four days later, but was arrested in Rabat alongside friend and fellow robber
Lee Murray
, who remains in jail in nearby Tiflet. In January 2008, Allen was extradited to the UK and subsequently sentenced to 18 years in prison.
Allen was released in 2016 and moved back to his roots in south-east London. But he relocated to Woodford with his partner and two younger children after a gunman opened fire at him and his pregnant daughter in the
doorway of their Woolwich home in September 2018
.
Ten months later, Allen almost died after those two bullets hit him as he stood in the kitchen of his Woodford haven.
Met Police
A bullet casing was found in the back garden of the property Paul Allen was living in when he was shot
Prosecutors argued the Ahearnes and Kelly were equally culpable in the plot to murder Allen - which involved a hired car, surveillance and unregistered pay-as-you-go phones.
"This was a meticulously researched and planned assassination attempt by a team of men well versed in the level of criminality to pull it off," prosecutor Michael Shaw KC said.
In discovering how the three knew where to find Allen, police would uncover their criminality stretched into mainland Europe.
The Geneva job and the Mayfair hotel sting
Just one month before the shooting, the Ahearne brothers and Kelly stood outside the Museum of Far Eastern Art in Geneva equipped with a sledgehammer, angle grinders and crowbars.
Within seconds of forcing their way through the front door, they shattered glass casings housing 14th Century Chinese Ming Dynasty antiques. Three items were seized - a rare pomegranate vase; a doucai-style wine cup and a porcelain bowl - and had a combined insured value of £2.8m.

data.title: Momentum seems to be building for Jared Isaacman to become NASA administrator
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary:
美国参议院批准了特朗普总统的大部分内阁成员后，焦点转向政府内阁以下级别的高级职位，其中包括备受瞩目的NASA局长人选。特朗普提名私人宇航员贾里德·艾萨克曼（Jared Isaacman）担任NASA局长，但提名尚未在参议院商业、科学和交通委员会获得听证。尽管艾萨克曼在航天界广受欢迎，并积极争取支持，但提名进展缓慢，主要障碍来自委员会主席、德州共和党参议员特德·克鲁兹（Ted Cruz）。克鲁兹对艾萨克曼曾捐助民主党人以及其对火星探索的兴趣表示不满。

尽管如此，艾萨克曼的提名仍被认为在轨道上。多位南部州长致信克鲁兹表达对艾萨克曼的支持，数十名前宇航员和商业航天联合会也发声支持。艾萨克曼已承诺解决利益冲突问题，如辞去其创办公司Shift4 Payments的职务并终止与SpaceX的协议。

尽管艾萨克曼与马斯克的关系可能引发争议，但其提名预计不会被彻底阻碍。由于参议院4月休会，听证会可能推迟到5月。NASA员工普遍希望有一位明确的领导人来带领机构前进，以应对特朗普政府带来的不确定性。

With the vast majority of President Donald Trump's cabinet members
now approved
by the US Senate, focus is turning to senior positions within the administration that are just below the cabinet level.
The administrator of NASA is among the most high-profile of these positions. Nearly four months ago
Trump nominated
private astronaut Jared Isaacman to become chief of the space agency, but he has yet to receive a hearing before the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
Almost immediately after his nomination, much of the space community fell in behind Isaacman, who has flown to space twice on private Crew Dragon missions, raised charitable funds, and is generally well-liked. Since then, Isaacman has worked to build support for his candidacy through conversations with people in the space community and officeholders.
However, publicly, not much has happened. This has raised questions within the space community about whether the nomination has stalled. Although some people have expressed concern about financial ties between Isaacman and SpaceX, according to multiple sources, the primary obstacle has been Ted Cruz, the Texas Republican who chairs the Senate committee.
Cruz is not happy that Isaacman has donated to Democrats in the past, and he is concerned that the private astronaut is more interested in Mars exploration than the Moon. Cruz also did not appreciate
Elon Musk's call
to end the life of the International Space Station early. The station is operated by NASA's field center, Johnson Space Center, in Houston, where Cruz lives.
Nomination on track
Nevertheless, despite the slower pace, people familiar with the nomination process say Isaacman's candidacy remains on track. And recently, there have been some public announcements that support this notion.
In early March, the governors of several southern US states, including Florida and Texas,
sent a letter to Cruz
expressing "strong support" for the swift confirmation of Isaacman. A notable absence from this letter was the governor of Alabama, Kay Ivey, where NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center is located. However, she also recently
sent Cruz a letter
praising Isaacman, calling him an "exceptional selection" to lead NASA. It is notable that the governors of all the US states with major human spaceflight activities have now lined up behind Isaacman.
Additionally, as part of the nomination process,
Isaacman has written a letter
to explain how he will disentangle his conflicts of interest, including resigning from the company he founded, Shift4 Payments, and stating that agreements between himself and SpaceX for the Polaris missions will be terminated.
A group of more than two dozen former astronauts from across the political spectrum also recently shared a letter sent to Cruz in support of Isaacman. "We believe that Jared Isaacman is uniquely qualified to lead NASA at the critical juncture," wrote the astronauts. And just this week, the Commercial Space Federation
issued a similar call for confirmation
.
This all appears to be part of an at least loosely coordinated campaign to push Cruz to schedule a hearing with Isaacman. A request for comment from Cruz, through the Senate committee he chairs, was not responded to.
NASA in need of a leader
So what will happen now?
Undoubtedly, Isaacman's ties to Musk will come up during the confirmation process, and potential conflicts of interest will be the source of some contention with Democratic senators.
SpaceX stands to benefit
from the Trump administration in myriad ways, including from NASA. At the same time, there is a general recognition that, when it comes to civil space, SpaceX has provided essential services to NASA at a significantly lower price than any other provider.
Therefore, although there may be some grumbling about Isaacman's conflicts, they are unlikely to be a killer. Cruz, too, has signaled privately that he is willing to move forward with the nomination. But it likely won't be soon. Due to recesses in April for Easter and Passover, there are limited opportunities for a confirmation hearing. Therefore, it seems most probable that Isaacman will not appear before Cruz's committee until May.
Is that a bad thing? If you ask people at NASA and within the industry, the answer is, generally, yes. Like other federal workers, the employees at NASA feel shell-shocked by the Trump administration's treatment of their jobs—the calls to resign, the requests for massive reductions in force, and concerns about budget cuts. There is a general sense that having a confirmed leader in Isaacman, who is viewed as dynamic and passionate about spaceflight, would provide clarity and confidence to get NASA moving ahead.

data.title: 931 Laid off at Block (Formerly Square) based on performance
data.author: darth_avocado
data.article_summary: Fintech company Block, owned by Jack Dorsey, announced the layoff of 931 employees, around 8% of its staff, in a leaked email seen by TechCrunch. Dorsey explained that the layoffs are part of organizational changes to align with strategic needs, improve performance, and flatten the company's hierarchy. The cuts are divided into three categories: 391 for strategic reasons, 460 for performance issues, and 80 managers as part of an effort to reduce hierarchy levels, with 193 managers moving to individual contributor roles. Additionally, Block is closing 748 open positions, except for those in advanced hiring stages or critical roles. Dorsey denied that the layoffs are financially motivated or related to AI replacement. This is Block's second major round of layoffs, following one in January 2024.
